CITY STICK features "community rounds" with a mix of challenges and jumps identified by our coaches and the community, followed by “challenger rounds” with head-to-head matchups where you and a friend will work on challenges side-by-side and try not to earn the letters that spell out "STICK"!  How long can you hold out?

About City Natives Workshop – Pumpkins!

Winter squash and pumpkins are key food sources for growers in our climate, providing a nutritious, late-season harvest that stores well into winter. Join us to harvest and taste-test two kinds of squash: New England Pie Pumpkin and Jamaican Pumpkin (a.k.a. Calabaza).

City Natives Plant Nursery is located at 30 Edgewater Dr. in Mattapan, a short walk from the Mattapan center bus and trolley stop. Street parking is also available. This workshop will take place during our weekly free food distribution initiative hosted by PanLyfe. Participants are invited to walk the grounds of the nursery before or after the workshop.

This workshop is free and open to all. No registration necessary. Email Lacey at lberg@thetrustees.org for weather related updates.

About Winter Solstice Tree ID Walk

Celebrate the winter solstice with a guided walk led by herbalist and arborist, Alex Klein, in the Leland St Cooperative Garden.

Even after fall winds have stripped them of their leaves, trees provide clues to their identification by way of their bark, leaf scars, and other individual characteristics. We will learn to point out key characteristics that will provide you the skills to identify any tree, even in the winter months. Warm wild herbal tea will be offered during the walk.

After the walk, participants are invited to join the garden community for their annual winter solstice celebration: welcome the Return of the Light by placing luminarias all around the garden. At 4:00 we will share a brief circle, offering an inclusive program with poems, songs, thoughts, or anything else you want to share.

Hot herbal tea will be served during the walk, and potluck style food and drink will be offered at the celebration afterwards.

This is a free event in partnership with the Boston Food Forest Coalition. Please register for weather releated updates.

The Leland St Cooperative Garden is located at 4 Leland St in Jamaica Plain, a short walk from the Forest Hills Orange Line Station. Street parking is available. The guided walk will be 100-200 meters around the grounds of the garden, with seating options available nearby.

BIPOC Climbers meetup

Central Rock Gym’s monthly meet up for BIPOC (Black, Indigenous, & People of Color) climbers expanding to our Cambridge location on the third Thursday of the month, this time on Thursday, November 19th! We invite you to attend and find climbing partners, new friends, and get climbing beta from those with similar techniques – whether you’re new to the sport or have been climbing for decades, we can all benefit from support on the walls!

This is a great event for those looking to climb for the first time or for those who are looking to make new climbing friends. This event is geared towards adults and older teenagers 18+. The meetup group is officially from 7-9pm, but you’re welcome to arrive early and stick around after.

*If you have not yet visited a Central Rock Gym location please fill out a participation agreement HERE.   Also, feel free to sign our bouldering orientation form. You will need to do it upon arrival if not done ahead of time. You will need facility access, either through a day pass, guest pass, or membership in order to participate.

Drop by the desk and we’ll help you find the rest of the group! This event is located at our Cambridge location at 170 Alewife Brook Pkwy. This is not located at the Harvard Square location, who offer their own meetup on a different date.

 

Our meetup will be hosted by Andrew Cao, a wonderful community member who has extensive experience working with affinity groups and has been climbing for about 3 years. Andrew loves painting, acro yoga, and playing with his cat. He also volunteers with the Adaptive Climbing Group at Bouldering Project, as well as with Boston Chinatown Neighborhood Center. Additionally, Andrew sometimes assists with the BIPOC nights at our Harvard Square location.

Join the Friends of the Boston Harborwalk as we explore the Brink's Robbery Tour - A Bank Heist, Waves of Molasses, and a Riot

Please join Mike Manning of the Friends of the Boston Harborwalk (FBHW) for a walking tour of the North End, the new William Felton “Bill” Russell Memorial Bridge, and the Charlestown Navy Yard. The tour will begin at the bocce courts located at 423 Commercial Street in Boston's North End and end at the USS Constitution Museum in the Charlestown Navy Yard. The bocce courts are located between Langone and Puopolo parks.

We'll tour the North End and visit the following sites: Edmund Hartt shipyard (1794), the Great Molasses Flood (1919), the Draft Riot of 1863 (on Prince Street), and the Brink's Robbery (1950) also on Prince Street. The tour will end at approximately 12:15 PM at the USS Constitution Museum.

Nearest T stop is North Station (nearest to the North End). Once in the Navy Yard, return-to-Boston options include the MBTA’s Charlestown-to-Long Wharf water ferry. The ferry departs from Pier 4 in the Navy Yard every thirty (30) minutes. The cross-harbor trip from Charlestown to Long Wharf is approximately ten (10) minutes.

The Friends of the Boston Harborwalk is an all-volunteer group affiliated with Boston Harbor Now (BHN). The group meets monthly to promote awareness, public enjoyment and local stewardship of Boston’s 43-mile Harborwalk. For more information on membership, please contact Mike Manning, Chair, at mmanning@bostonharbornow.org

Discover the Wharf District with a New Year's Eve afternoon walking tour by the Friends of the Harborwalk.

On New Year’s Eve day, join the Friends of the Harborwalk for a one-hour walking tour of Boston’s historic wharves led by Liz Nelson Weaver. Meet at 1:00 PM at Harbor Islands Visitor Center on the Greenway before proceeding to Long, Central, India, and Rowes wharves where you'll discover their rich history.


All are welcome, but please only RSVP if you plan to come, as space is limited. Registering for the event also allows us to contact you in case of inclement weather.


The Friends of the Boston Harborwalk is a volunteer group affiliated with Boston Harbor Now. The group meets monthly to promote awareness, public enjoyment and local stewardship of Boston’s 43-mile Harborwalk.


For more information on joining the group, please visit bostonharbornow.org/friends or contact Mike Manning, chair, at mmanning@bostonharbornow.org.

Ages 4-6
Join us for a 45 minute class once a week. Let us introduce your child to climbing! If your little one is ready to take on new heights, we are ready to help them scale the walls. Little Senders will help your child get used to and excited about climbing in a safety conscious and welcoming environment. They will learn basic skills and techniques and how to move on the wall. In addition your climber will also gather skills that translate out of the gym, including: a growing self-confidence, body awareness, cooperation, and communication skills.

This class is for all ability levels. Our low staff to student ratio allows us to provide a social environment while giving your child the individual attention that is needed to help them succeed.
